records.title: Does the reconstructed AIDL match the installed com.oplus.ipemanager?
records.summary: The reconstructed AIDL does not match ipemanager 16.13.0: same descriptor, but the transaction codes and part of the method set differ.
details: Known from code: the repository files are marked as cleaned reconstructions.
The route docs label every row of the interface reported until this is checked. The interface records in this database say verified because they match the repository's code, not a device.

Also unknown: whether the real interface has intensity, duration or waveform parameters, whether getSupportFeatureList has a transaction, and what the other calls mean (gap-oneplus-feature-semantics).

Owner decision, 2 Nov 2026: decompiling is allowed for this one check, on the copy of com.oplus.ipemanager pulled from the owner's own tablet. Only the pen-SDK interface classes are examined, the APK and decompiled output stay in research/local/, and only the descriptor, method names, transaction codes and signatures are recorded (CLAUDE.md). No mirror download is used.

Record: APK version and SHA-256, the aidl_check.py result (match, renumbered, signature differs, missing or extra, per method), and the descriptor seen at bind. The owner reviews any difference before the app's codes change.

records.title: Would Android drive a standard HID haptic pen?
records.summary: No Android API was found that sends HID Haptics page (0x0E) commands to a stylus. Whether Linux or Android route them at all is unknown.
details: If they did, a pen built to the Windows guide could work on Android without a vendor service.
Next step: check AOSP inputflinger and the Linux HID subsystem for Haptics page support.
records.basis: No source found on 2 Nov 2026.

records.title: If an app can bind, does the service accept its calls?
records.summary: The service may check the caller's UID, package or signature after a bind succeeds. Whether it does is unknown.
details: Reported, unconfirmed: a contributor suspects the client class PencilManagerUnitClient checks the calling app's package signature (src-revanced-180). If true, access depends on which app calls.
Reported, not checked: approved third-party apps authenticate per app through a OnePlus developer SDK (if-oneplus-partner-sdk).
Why it matters: it separates B2 (caller validation inside the service) from B1 (the Android permission), and B2 from B4 (the protocol).
Only reachable if the bind in gap-service-discovery-and-bind succeeds.

Next step: run step 3 of the isolating experiment: with the binder in hand, call a harmless query such as getPencilConnectState and see whether it returns or throws SecurityException or an auth error. The Route A PoC does this as its AUTHZ line.
Record: the call, the return value or the exact exception, its message and the layer.

ROM 2026-11-07: The ISdkAidlInterface implementation (obfuscated btadsorb.ble.g0, stub s3.d) performs no getCallingUid/package/signature checks per call; access control is the bind-time permission plus OCS hand-off (gap-oneplus-sdk-access).

ROM 2026-11-07: Transaction 0xFFFFFF with interface token com.oplus.ipemanager.PENCIL_CAPABILITY only records OCS auth data (byte, pid, uid, package) as the event event_ocs_auth; it does not gate later calls.

records.title: Does writing a captured value to the candidate characteristic make the pen buzz?
records.summary: The go or no-go for direct BLE: whether an ordinary app writing bytes copied from Notes' own traffic makes the pen vibrate.
details: Needs a captured value from gap-haptic-command-bytes and a candidate characteristic from gap-second-gatt-client-access. Do it only after gap-second-gatt-client-disruption shows a second connection is safe.
Write only bytes captured from Notes on this device. No fuzzing. BLE writes change hardware state, so ask the owner first.
If it works, the direct-BLE route is real: fill Stylo2GattProfile, write a Kotlin GattTransport, and set Availability.ble_protocol_verified.
Next step: with the inspector, write the bytes captured in the J scenarios to the candidate characteristic (plan-ble-independent-access-test, step 5).
Record: the characteristic, the bytes, with or without response, whether the pen vibrated, and any error.

Device attempt 1 2026-11-08: writing the ipemanager command bytes to char 58480001 (after subscribing to its NOTIFY) ALL succeeded at the GATT layer (status ok) but produced NO vibration. Sent: enable 2C 90 01 01 01, startVibration 2C 92 01 02 FF 02, setVibrationType 2C 94 02 0X 01 (types 0-3). So a bare write of the known bytes to the right characteristic is necessary but NOT sufficient. Caveats: (a) writes were Write-Without-Response, not Write-Request; (b) ipemanager's connect-time handshake was not replicated (gap-session-handshake); (c) bytes were the static-decompiled values (owner-approved), not Notes-captured (no-root snoop on this build yields no payloads). NOT a success (CLAUDE.md: works only if the pen vibrated).
records.basis: Transcribed from stylo2/docs/I-evidence-ledger.md (Q9) on 2 Nov 2026; not checked on a device.

records.title: What are the exact bytes for each profile, start and stop?
records.summary: No packet format is known for set-profile, start or stop. The docs deliberately invent none.
details: Known: nothing. No UUIDs, handles or encodings are recorded anywhere, on purpose.
Only meaningful if gap-haptic-over-gatt shows a GATT write.
The reconstructed interface has no intensity, duration, frequency or waveform parameter. Richer framing in the snoop would show otherwise (C, part 3).
Feeds: stylo2_ble::Stylo2GattProfile.encode and stylo2-oplus::wire::reported_code.
Next step: snoop scenarios 2 to 7, correlating the markers with the ATT writes (plan-hci-snoop-capture).
Record: for each scenario the handle, the characteristic UUID if resolvable, the opcode, the payload hex and whether the pen vibrated. Redact Bluetooth addresses.

Static 2026-11-08: candidate command bytes read from ipemanager o3/j.java (all GATT writes to one characteristic, prefix 0x2C): startVibration = '2C 92 01 02 FF 02'; setVibrationType = '2C 94 02 <type> <level+1>' (byte[3]=type 0-3, byte[4]=level+1); sendInstructionToPencil enable/disable = '2C 90 01 01 01' / '2C 90 01 01 00'; plus a wider 0x2C family (e.g. 2C 26..=feature, 2C 93/95/96/97..). These are the EXPECTED targets to match in the snoop. Per CLAUDE.md the on-device write must still use the snoop-captured value, not these bytes blindly.
Device 2026-11-08: target confirmed - the command characteristic is 58480001-5a6a-1122-3300-004095112200 (vendor service 58480000). The 2C-prefixed bytes write cleanly to it from an ordinary app.
records.basis: Static analysis of ipemanager 16.13.0 (g0.java, l0.java, o3/j.java) from the 16.0.10.600 ROM on 2026-11-08; host-side evidence, to be confirmed by an on-device HCI snoop and device test (CLAUDE.md). Earlier: Transcribed from stylo2/docs/I-evidence-ledger.md (Q5) on 2 Nov 2026; not checked on a device.

records.title: Is haptic control carried over GATT, or another channel?
records.summary: It is not known that the service reaches the pen's motor with a GATT write. The service name suggests it may use something else.
details: Known from the README: the service talks to the pen over Bluetooth. The pen's Bluetooth LE address reaches the tablet over the charging link (c-pen-attach-handshake).

The service component is .btadsorb.CoreService. The guide reads adsorb as the magnetic attach and charge relationship, so the path may be another L2CAP channel or something the service brokers. That reading is from the name only.
Nothing shows that the pen exposes a writable haptic characteristic.
Why it matters: it picks between direct BLE and the other routes (B4).

Next step: HCI snoop of Notes, one pencil stroke plus start and stop; see whether ATT writes line up with vibration (plan-hci-snoop-capture). Ask the owner first, because turning on the snoop log is a settings change.
Absence of a packet does not prove absence of a path.
Record: yes or no for ATT writes that line up with vibration. If no, what other traffic appears (L2CAP channel or other).

Static 2026-11-08: CONFIRMED (host side) that two of the three haptic calls DO reach the pen by BLE GATT write. setVibrationType (g0.java) and startVibration (l0.F0) write a BluetoothGattCharacteristic. BUT startFeedBackVibration/stop do NOT use GATT - they write touch node 38 via the vendor IOplusTouch HAL. So the transport is split: configurable vibration = BLE; writing-feedback on/off = touch node. Device/snoop still needed to confirm the pen actually buzzes from the GATT write.
records.basis: Static analysis of ipemanager 16.13.0 (g0.java, l0.java, o3/j.java) from the 16.0.10.600 ROM on 2026-11-08; host-side evidence, to be confirmed by an on-device HCI snoop and device test (CLAUDE.md). records.title: What is the protection level of com.oplus.permission.safe.IOT?
records.summary: On the Pad 3, com.oplus.permission.safe.IOT is signature|privileged and oplus.permission.OPLUS_COMPONENT_SAFE is signature; neither is held by an ordinary app or by shell.
details: Known: the repository's manifest requests it and the client checks it. The README calls it a restricted system permission that ordinary apps cannot be granted. The root module gets it by installing the app to /system/priv-app with a privapp-permissions allowlist.
Reported, not read: the level is at least privileged. Public system-app permission listings show the name on several com.oplus.* packages with no level.
Unknown: whether it is also signature-level, which would make even a privileged install need OnePlus's platform key (B0 and B1).
Why it matters: it decides whether the binder route is possible at all for an independent app.

Next step: run dumpsys package com.oplus.permission.safe.IOT and read protectionLevel from the framework permission XML. The service step of pad3_readout.py reads the level two ways; the raw commands are in plan-pad3-readout.
H also lists a B0 comparison of signers with apksigner verify --print-certs. CLAUDE.md rules out extracting vendor certificates, so ask the owner before that; the level alone answers this question.
Record: the protectionLevel text, the command or file it came from, and the firmware build. Also put the level in if-oplus-ipemanager.

ROM 2026-11-07: system_ext/framework/oplus-framework-res.apk (package 'oplus') declares com.oplus.permission.safe.IOT and com.oppo.permission.safe.IOT with protectionLevel 0x12 = signature|privileged (aapt2 dump xmltree).
ROM 2026-11-07: Consequence: an ordinary third-party app cannot hold it, so Android refuses an unprivileged bind to CoreService before ipemanager code runs.
ROM 2026-11-07: Still to do on the device: dumpsys package to confirm the level on the tablet's build.

Device-verified 2026-11-08 (dumpsys package): Permission com.oplus.permission.safe.IOT prot=signature|privileged (sourcePackage oplus); Permission oplus.permission.OPLUS_COMPONENT_SAFE prot=signature (sourcePackage oplus). safe.IOT held by com.oneplus.note and com.oplus.ipemanager, not by com.aige.hipaint. com.android.shell holds NEITHER permission - so a Shizuku/shell-backed app cannot hold the pen-haptics gates either.

records.title: How does an app join OnePlus's approved pen SDK?
records.summary: The supported route for third-party apps exists, but its availability, application process and terms are unknown.
details: Known: approved apps such as HiPaint authenticate with OnePlus through a developer SDK.
Unknown: whether the SDK is public, how to apply, what it checks and what it costs.
Next step: ask OnePlus developer relations or HiPaint's developer.

Route notes (Q11): the only non-root binder route, if B1 and B2 are closed, is official developer authorisation. Experiment: an enquiry to OnePlus or OPPO developer relations about authorising this app's package and signing certificate for the accessory service, and on what terms.
A desk web search on 2 Nov 2026 found no public official Pencil SDK, AAR or integration docs. That search cannot be repeated from this repository, and finding nothing does not show that none exists.
The route notes say it may need business terms and may not cover the Pad 3 and Stylo 2, and that no endpoint or credentials should be assumed.
Interoperability rule from the legal notes: use only the app's own signing certificate, never another developer's identity or keys.
ROM 2026-11-07: Third-party access runs through Open Capability Service (com.coloros.ocs.opencapabilityservice 16.0.8) with capability name IPE_PENCIL_CLIENT.

ROM 2026-11-07: Flow: the app presents an authCode; OCS verifies it; on success (error code 1001) OCS itself binds ipemanager's PENCIL_SDK action, reports the auth via transaction 0xFFFFFF, and hands ipemanager's SDK binder back to the app in a CapabilityInfo.

ROM 2026-11-07: The authCode is an offline ECDSA (SHA256withECDSA) signature by Oplus over a version byte, the caller's package name plus signing-certificate digest, permission bits and an optional expiry, checked against Oplus public keys on the device and cached locally. No network call in the auth module.

ROM 2026-11-07: So a valid code can only be issued by Oplus and is bound to one app identity; reusing another app's code is out of scope (CLAUDE.md: no credential reuse). The legitimate route is an IPE_PENCIL_CLIENT authorisation from OnePlus/Oplus.

HiPaint APK 2026-11-08 (static): corroborates the OCS route from the client side. HiPaint 6.4.2 (signer CN=huion) bundles com.oplus.ocs.base.* and requests capability IPE_PENCIL_CLIENT via AuthenticateCustomerBuilder, binding com.coloros.opencapabilityservice / OpenAuthenticateService (IServiceBroker.handleAuthentication). On success it receives an AuthResult carrying permit bits and a CapabilityInfo holding ipemanager's SDK binder, then calls ISdkAidlInterface directly.

HiPaint APK 2026-11-08 (static): ERROR_CODE_AUTHENTICATION_EXPIRED and 'incomplete credential' confirm the authCode is identity-bound and can expire. The credential is tied to HiPaint's own signing certificate (SHA-256 57e4c186...90879), so an interoperable app would need its OWN IPE_PENCIL_CLIENT authCode issued by Oplus for its own package and certificate - consistent with the no-credential-reuse rule.

HiPaint APK 2026-11-08 (full JADX decompile): the authCode is NOT in code - it is declared in the app's AndroidManifest as meta-data name="com.oplus.ocs.ipepencil.AUTH_CODE", value a base64 token (HiPaint's begins 'ATBEAiBc', 79 bytes; not reproduced in full - a vendor-signed token, not reused per CLAUDE.md).

HiPaint APK 2026-11-08: OCS service side com.oplus.ocs.authenticate.utils.h (PackageUtils) reads the caller's token via context.getPackageManager().getApplicationInfo(pkg, 128).metaData (flag 128 = GET_META_DATA); com.oplus.ocs.authenticate.utils.m verifies its ECDSA (SHA256withECDSA) signature against on-device Oplus public keys. Carried as AuthCodeInfo{authCode, enabled, expireIn}.

HiPaint APK 2026-11-08: token structure (base64-decoded, 79 bytes) = 0x01 version byte + DER ECDSA P-256 signature (30 44 ... , 70 bytes) + 8-byte permit/expiry trailer. Matches the OCS auth record format (version + signature over package + cert digest + permit bits + optional expiry).

HiPaint APK 2026-11-08: client side - h8/f BaseClient.getClientName()="IPE_PENCIL_CLIENT"; h8/h (OplusApi) Api "PencilManagerClient.API", client version 10000, brand-gated to OPPO/realme/OnePlus/oplus, checkAuthResult success = AuthResult.errorCode 1001 then ISdkAidlInterface.Stub.asInterface(CapabilityInfo.getBinder()); h8/e wraps the SDK (setVibrationType 0-3, getSupportFeatures, getVibrationSwitchState); l6/d is the IServiceBroker proxy (handleAuthentication = txn 1, OCS SDK version string "1.0.11").

HiPaint APK 2026-11-08: CORRECTION to the earlier ROM note - the app DOES present the authCode, but via its own manifest meta-data (read by OCS with GET_META_DATA), not passed over the bind transaction. The credential is bound to the caller's package (com.aige.hipaint) + signing cert (huion 57e4c186...) + permits; it is non-transferable. Interop path: obtain an Oplus-issued AUTH_CODE for OUR package + OUR cert and declare it in our manifest - there is no token to reuse.

Correction 2026-11-08: an earlier note here floated a possible non-OCS path via the touch node. That was wrong - the node-38 write is gated by oplus.permission.OPLUS_COMPONENT_SAFE (signature), so an ordinary app cannot use it either (see gap-oneplus-transport). Route C (OCS authCode) remains the only confirmed third-party route.

Device-verified 2026-11-08: com.aige.hipaint does NOT request com.oplus.permission.safe.IOT (dumpsys package), consistent with HiPaint reaching the SDK through OCS (authCode) rather than a direct IOT-gated bind.

records.title: What does the service send to the pen, and when?
records.summary: It is not known whether a haptic session is one start command with the pen playing on contact, or a stream of commands during writing.
details: The interface shape (set type, start, stop) and the Windows model both suggest the pen plays the texture locally on contact.
Next step: an HCI snoop log of a writing session in OnePlus Notes would show the pattern.
The nine capture scenarios, the recording schema and the tables are in plan-hci-snoop-capture. Scenarios 6 and 7 (feedback on, feedback off) show the command pattern.
A related question about the channel itself: gap-haptic-over-gatt.
ROM 2026-11-07: startFeedBackVibration/stopFeedBackVibration do not use Bluetooth: they call OplusTouchNodeManager.writeNodeFileByDevice(0, 38, "3") and (0, 38, "2"), i.e. touch-panel node 38.
ROM 2026-11-07: setVibrationType(int) writes a BLE GATT characteristic: a fixed command template with byte[3] = type and byte[4] = feedback level + 1, only when the pen connection state is 2.
ROM 2026-11-07: startVibration(int) is limited to the second-generation pencil (Stylo 2) and calls an internal routine still to be traced.
ROM 2026-11-07: Working hypothesis: writing feedback is switched on via the touch controller (digitiser link) while BLE configures pattern and strength.

Touch-node trace 2026-11-08 (ROM framework jars system/framework/oplus-framework.jar and oplus-services.jar, decompiled from the 16.0.10.600 system image): the full write path for node 38 is OplusTouchNodeManager.writeNodeFileByDevice(0,38,"3") [oplus-framework.jar, @hide system API; forwards only, no check] -> OplusActivityTaskManager binder -> ColorTouchNodeManagerService.writeNodeFileByDevice [com.android.server.wm, system_server] -> IOplusTouch HAL vendor.oplus.hardware.touch.IOplusTouch/default .touchWriteNodeFile(0,38,setInfo) -> sysfs node (path mapped inside the vendor HAL, not in the jars).

Touch-node trace 2026-11-08: node 38 is not one of the public OplusTouchNodeManager constants (those end at 22, plus debug 160-165); it is an internal nodeFlag the vendor HAL maps to a sysfs path. ipemanager has no special privilege for this call - it works because it can reach the hidden API and pass SELinux, not because of a permission.

Touch-node trace 2026-11-08 (CORRECTION of an earlier note in this record): node 38 IS permission-gated. The binder entry point is OplusActivityTaskManagerServiceEnhance.writeNodeFileByDevice, which calls enforceCallingPermission("oplus.permission.OPLUS_COMPONENT_SAFE", ...) BEFORE delegating to ColorTouchNodeManagerService (whose inner impl has no check). The earlier 'no caller gate' note read only the inner impl, not the Enhance wrapper the binder actually hits.

Touch-node trace 2026-11-08: oplus.permission.OPLUS_COMPONENT_SAFE is declared in oplus-framework-res.apk (package 'oplus') with protectionLevel 0x00000002 = signature. Only platform/oplus-signed apps can hold it; an ordinary third-party app cannot. So writing touch node 38 is signature-walled - the same class of barrier as the IOT/SDK bind. SELinux does allow an untrusted app to reach the service (activity_task_service is an app_api_service: 'allow untrusted_app_all app_api_service (service_manager (find))') and the @hide API is reflectable, but the signature permission is the hard wall. There is NO simpler non-OCS path for the feedback haptic; Route C (OCS authCode) remains the only third-party route. ipemanager works because it is platform-signed and holds OPLUS_COMPONENT_SAFE.

BLE command table 2026-11-08 (ipemanager o3/j.java + l0.java, static): pen commands are GATT writes to characteristic f2707l0, all prefixed 0x2C. startVibration (l0.F0) writes f5605p = '2C 92 01 02 FF 02' (fixed), gated only by isFunctionVibrationEnable + pen connected (no app-identity check at this layer because the SDK binder is already reached via the signature/OCS gate). setVibrationType writes f5606q template '2C 94 02 <type> <level+1>' (byte[3]=type, byte[4]=level+1). sendInstructionToPencil toggles '2C 90 01 01 01'/'...00' by the settings_enable_oppo_pencil setting. Pencil-type map includes 2 = OnePlus Pencil 2 Pro (Stylo 2). Recorded as constants; writing them to a pen is a device action needing owner approval and only with bytes captured from Notes (CLAUDE.md).

Device-verified 2026-11-08: the node-38 gate oplus.permission.OPLUS_COMPONENT_SAFE is prot=signature on the tablet (dumpsys package), confirming the touch-node write path is signature-walled for ordinary apps.

records.title: Which firmware directory does each tablet need?
records.summary: Partly answered: the directory is named after the tablet's ro.boot.prjname. Still unknown: which number in each pair is Chinese and which global, and what the converted Pad 3 reports.
details: Answered: jjhitel's fix creates /odm/firmware/wireless_pen/<ro.boot.prjname>/, and users report it restores the pen.
Known numbers: 23926, 23927, 23976, 23978 (Pad Pro / Pad 2); 24926, 24976 (Pad 2 Pro family).

On the Pad 3: run getprop ro.boot.prjname and ls -lR /odm/firmware/wireless_pen/, hash each cps8601_firmware.bin, and check dmesg | grep cps8601 after attaching the pen. The commands are listed in research/docs/pen-attach-handshake.md.
Also unknown: how 24976's firmware compares with 24926's, and whether KernelSU mounts a module's top-level odm/ folder.
To settle how the driver builds the path, read the GPL source of oplus_wireless_pen in OnePlus's kernel release.

records.title: Which setVibrationType integers give which feel?
records.summary: The profile integers are the enum's declaration order, and which feel each one produces on the pen has not been checked.
details: Known from code: the client sends the enum ordinal (Pencil 0, Eraser 1, Ballpoint 2, Pen 3, FUNCTION_VIBRATION 4), and the Rust mapping reported_code returns the same values. The code comments and route docs warn that declaration order should not be trusted as the wire value.
The README says the presets come from analysis of the stock Notes app. That is not a check on a device.
Unknown: whether the service uses these integers as given, what 4 does for setVibrationType, and whether 0 to 4 are all valid.
The PoC spinner covers 0 to 3. Matrix test 6 says 0 to 3. G section 7 and C section 1.5 say 0 to 4.
C and a code comment call FUNCTION_VIBRATION (4) a feedback mode rather than a profile. Nothing confirms it (gap-oneplus-feature-semantics).

Next step: call setVibrationType(n) for n = 0 to 4 on a working binding (authorised), start feedback each time, and record which feel each n produces; or read the bytes from the snoop; then correct stylo2-oplus::wire::reported_code. Only the PoC's own calls are in scope; do not change the profile integers in code without device evidence.
Record: for each n, the feel in plain words and whether the pen vibrated.

Also unknown: whether an ordinary app sees the pen's advertisement or address at all (matrix tests 1 and 2), and whether Companion Device Manager would help.

records.title: Can an ordinary app discover and bind the pen service?
records.summary: No source shows what Android does when an app without the IOT permission looks for, or binds, com.oplus.ipemanager.
details: Known: the repository's own client checks the permission first and stops with PermissionDenied before it calls bindService, so it never shows what the platform does.
The README says any other app is refused. That is its statement, not a test result.

Unknown: whether the service is exported and visible to an ordinary app, whether it has a bind-time android:permission, and whether bindService returns true, returns false or throws SecurityException.
A failure at discovery points to export or visibility (B2). A SecurityException or false at bind points to B1 or a bind-time permission.

Next step: run steps 1 and 2 of the isolating experiment: queryIntentServices for com.oplus.ipemanager.ACTION.PENCIL_SDK, then bindService and wait for onServiceConnected. The Route A PoC does both and logs exported and the service's bind permission for each match.
Record: number of matches, exported, bind permission, the bindService result or the exact exception and message, and the descriptor at connect.

ROM 2026-11-07: CoreService (com.oplus.ipemanager.btadsorb.CoreService) is exported, runs in process :ble and is protected by android:permission=com.oplus.permission.safe.IOT (signature|privileged), so an ordinary app's bind is refused by the platform.
ROM 2026-11-07: CoreService.onBind returns the SDK binder for com.oplus.ipemanager.ACTION.PENCIL_SDK without any further caller check.

Device-verified 2026-11-08 (partial): the bind-time gate is confirmed - safe.IOT is signature|privileged and no ordinary app (incl. shell) holds it. The unprivileged-bind OUTCOME itself was not tested (no PoC run), so the 'bind refused' conclusion stays inferred-from-verified, not directly observed.

records.title: Is there a session handshake before the first haptic?
records.summary: The pen may need a session setup or per-command authentication before it accepts haptic commands. Not known.
details: Known: nothing. This is the B4 hypothesis.
If a handshake exists, it is modelled as an Initialising state (the target lifecycle in H) and reproduced before commands. An app-level authentication would make direct BLE unlikely.
Next step: inspect snoop scenario 9, the initial connection from a powered-off pen with the snoop already running, for any exchange before the first haptic (plan-hci-snoop-capture).
Record: direction, opcode, handle, payload, and notes on handshake, CCCD subscribe, MTU or PHY. Redact Bluetooth addresses.

Static 2026-11-08: there is likely an enable/session step. ipemanager gates GATT writes on pen connection state == 2, and G() sendInstructionToPencil writes '2C 90 01 01 01' when settings_enable_oppo_pencil is set (vs '...00'). Capture 9 of plan-hci-snoop-capture (fresh connect) should show whether a 2C 90 enable (or other handshake) must precede the first haptic. Still open: whether a second, independent GATT client must repeat it.

Elevated 2026-11-08: direct writes to 58480001 did not buzz the pen, so a connect-time handshake/session is the leading missing piece. In l0.java, G0() (sendInstructionToPencil, writes 2C 90... gated by settings_enable_oppo_pencil) is invoked from many connection-state handlers on connect, and more f2707l0 writes run during init. The pen may also need Write-Request (not no-response) and/or specific notify subscriptions answered. Separately, the writing-feedback buzz is driven by touch node 38 (signature-walled), so BLE setVibrationType may only CONFIGURE the pattern - startVibration (2C 92) is the only BLE trigger and it did not buzz either. Open: replicate the full handshake; try Write-Request; determine if any buzz is reachable over BLE alone or whether it fundamentally needs the touch-node path.
